question: Which of these actions breaks patient confidentiality during a home visit?

options.A: Asking a conscious adult patient before sharing details with family
options.B: Locking your paper notes inside a secure bag while traveling
options.C: Writing your visit notes right after leaving the patient's home
options.D: Gossip about the patient's diagnosis with neighbors outside the house

explanation: Spot on! Patient privacy is sacred. Discussing health details with outsiders like neighbors is a serious breach of professional ethics.

question: Which data collection method involves talking directly with trusted village leaders about local health issues?

options.A: Laboratory blood screenings
options.B: Key informant interviews
options.C: Direct environmental observation
options.D: Reviewing census registers

explanation: Key informants are knowledgeable community figures who provide deep insight into local health behaviors and needs. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of bowel preparation before rectovaginal fistula surgery?

options.A: To reduce fecal load and minimize infection risk
options.B: To increase blood pressure during the operation
options.C: To stretch the vaginal walls for easier access
options.D: To test the kidneys for dye clearance

explanation: Clearing the bowel reduces stool contamination at the surgical site, lowering the risk of postoperative wound infection and failure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h6)

question: What triggers the release of the hormone cholecystokinin (CCK) during digestion?

options.A: The drop in pH inside the stomach lumen
options.B: The presence of fats and proteins in the duodenum
options.C: The smell of food before it enters the mouth
options.D: The arrival of water in the large intestine

explanation: When fats and proteins hit the first part of your small intestine (duodenum), CCK gets released. It tells the gallbladder to squeeze out bile and the pancreas to release its enzymes!

question: A patient scheduled for a spinal tap is currently taking warfarin for a heart condition. What is the nurse's best action?

options.A: Notify the doctor immediately about the bleeding risk
options.B: Proceed with the tap quickly before the next drug dose
options.C: Apply a hot pack to the lower back to thin the blood
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink extra water right away

explanation: Great job! Blood thinners increase the risk of bleeding into the spinal canal, so the doctor must be informed right away.

question: What is the main job of the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities?

options.A: To manage shipping ports and maritime trade
options.B: To enforce laws protecting the rights and inclusion of persons with disabilities
options.C: To provide military combat training for citizens
options.D: To oversee the building of telecom masts

explanation: Correct! This commission exists to make sure individuals living with disabilities have their rights protected and are fully included in society.

question: A patient with severe salpingitis, high fever, and nonstop vomiting is admitted for IV antibiotics. What is the main reason for hospital admission?

options.A: Need for immediate total removal of both fallopian tubes
options.B: Requirement for daily pelvic ultrasound monitoring at bedside
options.C: Desire to isolate the patient from all household family members
options.D: Inability to tolerate oral medications due to severe nausea

explanation: If a patient can't keep pills down because of vomiting, oral meds won't work. Bringing them in for IV treatment ensures the drugs actually get into their system.

question: Which two main proteins make up the tiny filaments inside a muscle sarcomere?

options.A: Collagen and elastin
options.B: Actin and myosin
options.C: Troponin and calcium
options.D: Myoglobin and hemoglobin

explanation: Actin (the thin one) and myosin (the thick one) are the dynamic duo inside your muscles that slide together to create movement. Brilliant! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h2)

question: What is another common name for the normal bacteria and microbes living on and inside the human body?

options.A: Human microbiota
options.B: Somatic organisms
options.C: Pathogenic colonies
options.D: Acellular particles

explanation: You've got this! 'Human microbiota' is just the scientific term for the friendly community of microbes that call our bodies home. Every healthy person has them!

question: What is a major reason eating disorders often start during the teenage years?

options.A: The permanent loss of taste buds during puberty
options.B: Intense body image concerns combined with rapid physical changes
options.C: Excessive physical exercise required by school curriculums
options.D: A complete lack of appetite caused by hormonal stabilization

explanation: You're doing great! Rapid body changes can make teens super self-conscious, sometimes triggering unhealthy eating habits.

question: What is the main goal of managing a healthcare facility's infrastructure?

options.A: Reducing the total number of clinical staff employed in the hospital
options.B: Minimizing the purchase of new medical and diagnostic equipment
options.C: Ensuring physical assets support patient safety and staff productivity
options.D: Maximizing the financial profit of the facility above all else

explanation: Think of infrastructure management as making sure the building and equipment help nurses care for patients safely and smoothly without unnecessary stress!

question: Which of these is a classic example of a microvascular complication of diabetes?

options.A: Peripheral stroke
options.B: Carotid atherosclerosis
options.C: Diabetic retinopathy
options.D: Coronary artery disease

explanation: Retinopathy targets the tiny capillaries inside the eyes, making it a classic microvascular ('small vessel') complication.

question: Which objective is a primary focus of a child day care centre?

options.A: Promoting early socialization and cognitive play
options.B: Issuing primary school completion certificates
options.C: Treating severe infectious disease outbreaks
options.D: Providing formal university entrance training

explanation: Child day care focuses heavily on early childhood development through structured play, social interaction, and cognitive activities. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h2)

question: What is a major advantage of using a correlational research design?

options.A: It eliminates all possible confounding variables
options.B: It requires no statistical calculations or math skills
options.C: It proves definitively that one variable causes another
options.D: It can be used when experimental manipulation is impossible

explanation: You nailed it! Correlational studies let us explore real-world topics safely, even when changing things on purpose would be unethical.

question: An abnormal hole between the two lower chambers (ventricles) of the heart is known as:

options.A: Ventricular septal defect
options.B: Atrial septal defect
options.C: Aortic stenosis
options.D: Mitral regurgitation

explanation: A ventricular septal defect (VSD) is just an opening in the wall (septum) separating the right and left lower chambers.

question: What should a nursing team do if their evaluation shows a new practice didn't improve patient results?

options.A: Hide the results from management so nobody gets blamed
options.B: Reassess how it was applied or look for alternative evidence
options.C: Stop all research activities in the hospital permanently
options.D: Keep using it anyway to avoid admitting any failure

explanation: Well thought out! Science is a journey of trial and learning. If it didn't work out, we review our steps or search for a better approach.

question: What is the main purpose of a healthcare referral pathway?

options.A: To ensure patients never leave their local village clinic
options.B: To punish nurses who cannot solve complex surgical problems
options.C: To connect patients to higher levels of care when needs exceed primary facilities
options.D: To increase the financial profit of private pharmacies

explanation: When a patient's condition is too complex for a primary health post (like needing a C-section or major surgery), a referral pathway ensures they get smoothly transferred to a general hospital.

question: What happens to sealed sharps containers after they are filled in the hospital?

options.A: They are washed out with soap and water for reuse in the children's ward
options.B: They are emptied into general waste bins for easy community recycling
options.C: They are encapsulated in concrete or buried in engineered sanitary landfills
options.D: They are dissolved entirely using basic liquid hand sanitizers

explanation: Well done! Sealing them in concrete or deep landfills ensures nobody gets accidentally poked by old needles later.

question: When must a nurse choose soap and water over an alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.B: Before entering a patient room for vital signs
options.C: After touching an intact patient gown
options.D: Immediately before administering oral medication

explanation: Alcohol rubs do not clean away physical dirt or certain spore-forming bacteria effectively, requiring mechanical washing with soap and water. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is a common misconception about herbal and complementary medications?

options.A: They can only be bought with a doctor's prescription
options.B: They are chemically identical to synthetic antibiotics
options.C: They never interact with standard hospital drugs
options.D: They are completely harmless because they are natural

explanation: Patients often think natural means safe, but herbs contain active chemicals that can cause serious side effects or drug interactions. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h5)

question: When is skeletal traction usually taken off?

options.A: When the patient is ready for surgery, casting, or healing allows
options.B: As soon as the patient gets bored on bed rest
options.C: When the pin site develops normal crusting
options.D: Exactly 24 hours after the pin was put in

explanation: You got it! Skeletal traction is a temporary helper. It comes off once definitive care like surgery or a cast takes over, or when the bone is stable enough.

question: Why must nurse leaders assess the current environment before trying to change the culture?

options.A: To comply with building safety codes and fire regulations
options.B: To find out which individual staff members need immediate firing
options.C: To gather baseline data and identify specific problem areas
options.D: To calculate the exact budget required for annual staff bonuses

explanation: You're right! Assessment helps leaders see what's really happening so they can target actual problems rather than just guessing.

question: Which home care instruction is most critical for a patient who just had a liver biopsy?

options.A: Call the clinic or return if you feel severe shoulder or belly pain
options.B: Go for long daily jogs to boost blood circulation
options.C: Scrub the tiny wound hard with soap immediately
options.D: Take aspirin every morning to prevent clots

explanation: You got it! Severe pain can be an early warning sign of internal bleeding or other complications, so patients must report it right away.

question: What is the main limitation of relying solely on national laws to stop harmful traditional practices?

options.A: Courts are legally forbidden from hearing domestic abuse cases
options.B: Laws cannot change deep social beliefs without community engagement
options.C: Law enforcement officers are exempt from handling family matters
options.D: International treaties always override local criminal statutes

explanation: Legislation provides penalties, but if the community still values the tradition, practices simply go underground. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard nursing responsibility during EENT exams?

options.A: Prescribing the specific antibiotic treatment plan independently
options.B: Setting up good lighting and positioning for the doctor
options.C: Watching out for any bad reactions to local numbing meds
options.D: Explaining the procedure to help the patient relax

explanation: Nurses prep patients, assist during the check, and keep things safe, but prescribing medications is outside the nursing scope of practice.

question: Which blood test is commonly checked to assess a patient's nutrition before surgery?

options.A: Serum albumin
options.B: Red blood cell count
options.C: Blood glucose
options.D: Platelet count

explanation: You got it! Serum albumin is a classic protein marker we use to check a surgical patient's nutritional reserves.

question: An adult child is crying and demanding that staff restart all life support for a dying parent, even though the parent has a clear living will stating otherwise. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Act as an advocate for the patient by gently reminding the family of the documented wishes
options.B: Tell the family that their opinion does not matter at all in the hospital
options.C: Immediately follow the child's orders to stop the family conflict
options.D: Call hospital security to remove the family member from the room

explanation: The nurse bridges the gap with compassion, offering emotional support while firmly upholding the documented autonomy of the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h7)

question: A nurse wears gloves and a face shield while cleaning a bloody wound on a patient with an unknown diagnosis. What is the nurse practicing?

options.A: Active surveillance
options.B: Tertiary prevention
options.C: Standard precautions
options.D: Airborne quarantine

explanation: Brilliant! Treating every patient's body fluids as potentially infectious by using barriers like gloves is the golden rule of standard precautions.

question: A community nurse is inspecting a pregnant woman's home delivery kit. Which item is UNNECESSARY or unsafe for newborn cord care?

options.A: A clean, sterile razor blade for cutting the cord
options.B: Traditional herbal mixture applied directly to the cut cord
options.C: Clean thread to tie off the umbilical cord securely
options.D: Soap and clean water for thorough handwashing

explanation: Applying unsterile substances like herbal mixtures to the umbilical cord introduces bacteria and causes severe neonatal infections like tetanus. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h2)

question: During a routine speculum exam, you notice a red, velvety patch on a patient's cervix. What is your priority action?

options.A: Preparing the patient for emergency surgical removal of the cervix
options.B: Assisting with obtaining a Pap smear and screening tests to rule out dysplasia or infection
options.C: Instructing the patient to avoid all fluid intake for twelve hours
options.D: Administering intravenous antibiotics immediately without testing

explanation: Always prioritize screening! You can't tell what a red patch is just by looking at it, so a Pap smear or swab is necessary to check for infections or abnormal cells.

question: Which bacteria is most famous for causing fast, painful infections after a cat or dog bite?

options.A: Pasteurella multocida
options.B: Clostridium tetani
options.C: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.D: Escherichia coli

explanation: Pasteurella lives happily in cat and dog mouths. Once introduced through a bite, it quickly causes sharp pain, redness, and swelling.

question: What is the primary purpose of community entry in the mobilisation cycle?

options.A: Collecting taxes from local market traders
options.B: Building a permanent health clinic building
options.C: Conducting mass vaccinations for all children
options.D: Gaining social and legal acceptance from local leaders

explanation: Community entry is all about introducing yourself, getting permission, and building trust with local leaders before starting any work. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h3)

question: What is the very first thing you must do before putting on examination gloves?

options.A: Open the outer wrapper
options.B: Perform hand hygiene
options.C: Check the patient's skin
options.D: Wipe down your work table

explanation: Always clean your hands first! Putting gloves on unwashed hands traps germs right against your skin.

question: What does a sustainable elimination strategy primarily depend upon for long-term success?

options.A: Keeping all intervention data strictly secret from the public
options.B: Relying entirely on short-term foreign donor funding
options.C: Embedding prevention into national policies and health training
options.D: Punishing communities rather than engaging in dialogue

explanation: Sustainability means the work continues routinely through local systems, education, and government policy without fading away. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h8)

question: A patient after abdominal surgery tries to avoid taking deep breaths because it hurts. What complication are they most likely heading toward?

options.A: Atelectasis
options.B: Muscle contractures
options.C: Pressure ulcers
options.D: Renal failure

explanation: Well done! Shallow breathing stops the tiny air sacs (alveoli) from opening up fully, which can cause them to collapse and lead to atelectasis or pneumonia. Encouraging deep breaths is key!

question: Why are mid-range servers (minicomputers) so helpful in hospital departments like the laboratory?

options.A: They efficiently handle department-specific data traffic and device integration
options.B: They act as portable bedside charting tools for individual nurses
options.C: They predict global disease outbreaks using atmospheric data
options.D: They replace the need for electrical power outlets in the ward

explanation: You nailed it. Departments like the lab generate lots of specific results, and mid-range servers are perfect for managing that local workflow without slowing down the whole hospital.

question: Why is strict sterile technique so vital when handling invasive lines in the ICU?

options.A: To speed up the healing of superficial skin bruises
options.B: To prevent introducing bacteria directly into the bloodstream
options.C: To reduce the cost of buying hospital cleaning supplies
options.D: To ensure the medical dressings stick to the skin longer

explanation: Invasive lines open up a direct highway past the skin. If we aren't super clean, germs can dive straight into the blood and cause dangerous infections like sepsis. Excellent hygiene saves lives!

question: Why do certain odors often trigger strong emotional memories?

options.A: Because the olfactory cortex connects directly to the limbic system
options.B: Because smell signals are processed first by the visual association area
options.C: Because taste buds share nerve pathways with the emotional centers
options.D: Because the thalamus amplifies scent signals during sleep

explanation: The limbic system is the emotional and memory center of the brain, and its direct link to smell explains this strong connection. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h5)

question: A patient catches a hookworm infection after walking barefoot on damp, contaminated soil. How did the parasite get in?

options.A: Inhalation of airborne cysts
options.B: An infected insect bite
options.C: Direct skin penetration
options.D: Feco-oral contamination

explanation: Spot on! Some worm larvae are crafty enough to burrow right through the soft skin of bare feet. Always wear your shoes!

question: When are outbreaks of water-borne diseases like cholera most common in Nigeria?

options.A: In the middle of the hot dry summer months
options.B: During the rainy season when floods overwhelm sanitation
options.C: Right after major harvesting periods end
options.D: During the dry harmattan season when dust increases

explanation: Heavy rains wash surface waste into shallow wells and boreholes, spreading contamination rapidly during the rainy season. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is improvement fatigue in a clinical setting?

options.A: Exhaustion caused by lifting heavy patients without mechanical assistance
options.B: Feeling overwhelmed by an endless stream of new mandates and quality targets
options.C: Physical tiredness caused by walking too many miles during a night shift
options.D: A rare muscle disease that affects nurses working in intensive care

explanation: Too many overlapping projects exhaust staff mental energy, causing them to resist any further operational changes. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is it dangerous to give sugary drinks to an unconscious patient with low blood sugar?

options.A: The stomach will reject all sugary liquids
options.B: It can cause choking or enter the lungs
options.C: It will immediately cause a diabetic coma
options.D: It takes three days for the body to digest it

explanation: An unconscious patient cannot protect their airway. Giving them fluids by mouth can cause aspiration, sending liquid straight into their lungs. Safety first!

question: What exactly is a windshield survey in community health?

options.A: Interviewing automobile drivers about local road accidents
options.B: Inspecting vehicles used for transporting emergency patients
options.C: Observing community conditions firsthand while moving through the area
options.D: Testing the window glass quality of local health clinics

explanation: Imagine driving or walking slowly through a neighborhood, looking at housing, open drainage, and market areas with your own eyes. That's a windshield survey!

question: What happens if the body fails to maintain proper immune tolerance?

options.A: Innate barriers permanently lose their ability to secrete mucus
options.B: Primary lymphoid organs immediately stop producing white blood cells
options.C: The immune system attacks the body's own healthy cells and tissues
options.D: The body becomes completely defenseless against minor viral colds

explanation: Correct! When tolerance fails, the body stops recognizing 'self' and starts an autoimmune attack on its own healthy organs.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge faced by local emergency responders in Nigeria?

options.A: Abundant surplus of modern emergency helicopters in every local clinic
options.B: Poor inter-agency coordination during major crises
options.C: Delays in communication channels
options.D: Inadequate funding for disaster preparedness

explanation: Spot on! Local clinics usually struggle with shortages rather than having an overabundance of expensive equipment like helicopters.

question: What is the primary goal of health promotion?

options.A: Enabling people to increase control over and improve their health
options.B: Providing free medications to rural communities
options.C: Treating acute diseases in hospital settings
options.D: Isolating individuals with infectious conditions

explanation: Health promotion focuses on empowering individuals and communities to manage and better their overall well-being rather than just curing sickness. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the main cause of painful breast engorgement in the first few days after giving birth?

options.A: Bacterial infection spreading through the lactiferous ducts
options.B: Blockage of the nipple pores by dried colostrum
options.C: A sudden drop in maternal oxytocin during feedings
options.D: Vascular congestion and the initial rush of milk coming in

explanation: Engorgement happens because blood flow to the breasts increases, fluid builds up, and milk rushes in all at once. It's a traffic jam of fluids!

question: Which assessment finding is a reliable indicator of poor peripheral tissue perfusion?

options.A: Warm and pink extremities
options.B: Cool, pale, or bluish skin
options.C: Rapid and clear speech
options.D: Bounding radial pulse strength

explanation: Cold, pale, or cyanotic skin often means blood flow to the skin and outer tissues is reduced. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h7)

question: Why do we say out-of-pocket spending is a rough deal for patients?

options.A: It forces families to pay directly at the point of care, leading to financial hardship
options.B: It requires too much paperwork for hospital administrators
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for government hospitals
options.D: It increases the overall supply of essential medicines too quickly

explanation: Paying cash right at the hospital door can wipe out a family's savings overnight when a sudden sickness hits. That's why health insurance is so important!

question: A nurse planning a sensitization meeting in a rural village should use which method to reach the most people?

options.A: Academic lectures delivered in medical English
options.B: Complex medical journals published online
options.C: Town hall meetings and local drama in the native language
options.D: Written pamphlets distributed to university students

explanation: Using local languages and engaging formats like drama ensures that everyone, including those who cannot read, can understand the message. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h3)

question: During a home visit, a nurse notices a psychiatric client is also suffering from severe untreated malnutrition and extreme poverty. What is the best next step?

options.A: Discharge the client from psychiatric care permanently
options.B: Tell the family to borrow money immediately from a bank
options.C: Refer the client to social welfare and appropriate support agencies
options.D: Ignore the poverty because nurses only treat mental symptoms

explanation: Holistic community care requires linking clients with social welfare services when poverty and malnutrition impact their health. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is the very first practical step when doing medication reconciliation during a home visit?

options.A: Calling the local pharmacy to order a fresh supply of all tablets
options.B: Gathering all current medication bottles and packages into one place
options.C: Asking the doctor to rewrite every prescription from the beginning
options.D: Throwing away any medicine that does not have a readable label

explanation: You got it! You have to round up all the medications first so you can actually see what the patient has and is taking.

question: What is the main job of the cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical brain circuit in OCD?

options.A: Controlling voluntary muscle movement in the upper extremities
options.B: Producing visual images during rapid eye movement sleep
options.C: Filtering sensory information and regulating behavioral habits
options.D: Regulating body temperature and fluid balance in the kidneys

explanation: You nailed it! When this pathway has trouble filtering routine signals, the brain gets stuck in repetitive loops of thoughts and actions.

question: A rural health clinic receives a dedicated increase in operational funding. What improvement should the nurse expect to see first?

options.A: A surplus of specialized neurosurgeons
options.B: Decreased need for community health education
options.C: Availability of open-heart surgery equipment
options.D: Reliable vaccine storage and basic medical supplies

explanation: Primary health care priorities focus on basic infrastructure, vaccines, and essential medications rather than highly specialized surgical gear. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h3)

question: Which of these terms specifically refers to the human being experiencing this phase of growth?

options.A: Adolescent
options.B: Youth
options.C: Adolescence
options.D: Pubescence

explanation: The adolescent is the actual person, while terms like adolescence and youth describe the time periods or social stages.

question: An adult patient with dysphagia is getting ready to eat lunch. What is the best position for this patient?

options.A: Lying completely flat on their back
options.B: Lying on their side with knees bent
options.C: Reclining at a comfortable 30-degree angle
options.D: Sitting upright at a 90-degree angle

explanation: An upright posture uses gravity to help food move safely down the esophagus instead of entering the airway. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h6)

question: A nurse wants to study past unconscious ICU dreams, but no records exist. Which research requirement is missing?

options.A: Clinical significance
options.B: Availability of data
options.C: Ethical clearance
options.D: Personal interest

explanation: If the information you need doesn't exist or can't be gathered, you won't be able to carry out that specific study.

question: Which IPC measure is considered the single most effective action to prevent germ spread?

options.A: Closing all windows in the house
options.B: Frequent hand hygiene
options.C: Spraying disinfectant on the skin
options.D: Taking daily vitamin supplements

explanation: Regular and proper handwashing with soap and water or alcohol rub is the cornerstone of all infection prevention protocols. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h5)

question: Which patient condition means Oral Rehydration Therapy is unsafe, requiring IV fluids instead?

options.A: Mild watery diarrhea with normal skin turgor
options.B: Profound hypovolemic shock with altered consciousness
options.C: Low-grade fever and mild nausea
options.D: Frequent loose stools without vomiting

explanation: If a patient is in shock or unconscious, they cannot swallow safely. They need quick intravenous fluids to restore their blood pressure.

question: Why do nurses rely on a structured sorting system like START during a disaster?

options.A: It removes emotional bias and prevents spending too much time on a single patient
options.B: It guarantees that every single injured person will recover completely
options.C: It allows nurses to perform major surgeries outside their normal scope
options.D: It eliminates the need for any documentation or patient tracking

explanation: Under intense pressure, standard systems help nurses make quick, objective choices so they can help the greatest number of people.

question: A nurse finishes dressing a wound soaked with infected pus. Where should the soiled gauze dressing be discarded?

options.A: Cardboard medication box
options.B: General recycling container
options.C: Yellow infectious waste bag
options.D: Black domestic waste bin

explanation: Infectious clinical waste containing body fluids goes into the yellow bag to prevent the spread of pathogens. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h5)

question: What does 'monitoring' primarily involve in community health programs?

options.A: Continuous tracking of service uptake and activities
options.B: Waiting until a five-year grant period finishes
options.C: Changing the geographic location of the clinic daily
options.D: Firing staff members who fail to meet quotas

explanation: Monitoring is an ongoing process of tracking day-to-day activities and service delivery metrics. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h7)

question: You find a weeping trader sitting alone after a market fire. What is your best first move using PFA?

options.A: Insist that the trader explain the exact sequence of how the fire started
options.B: Approach calmly, offer a safe space, and listen to immediate practical concerns
options.C: Refer the trader directly to a psychiatric hospital for formal psychotherapy
options.D: Administer a strong oral sedative to prevent immediate panic attacks

explanation: Great nurse instinct! PFA isn't about interrogation or rushing to drugs. It's about a calm, safe presence and listening to what they need right now.

question: In Dorothea Orem's theory, what exactly does a 'self-care deficit' mean?

options.A: The hospital has run out of supplies needed for patient hygiene
options.B: The doctor has forbidden the patient from eating solid foods
options.C: The patient's need for self-care is greater than their ability to do it
options.D: The nurse refuses to help the patient walk around the ward

explanation: You nailed it. A self-care deficit simply happens when the care a person needs is higher than what they are currently able to pull off by themselves.

question: Where is the prostate gland located in the male body?

options.A: Directly behind the urinary bladder
options.B: Inside the shaft of the penis near the tip
options.C: Wrapped around the urethra below the bladder
options.D: Attached directly to the outer surface of the testes

explanation: The prostate sits right under the bladder and encircles the upper urethra. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the very first step in the formal healthcare planning process?

options.A: Evaluating alternatives
options.B: Buying equipment
options.C: Setting objectives
options.D: Punishing staff

explanation: You must first know what you want to achieve by setting clear objectives before looking at options. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why is it always smart to let a friend read your draft before you submit it?

options.A: It guarantees that your study will receive immediate funding
options.B: Writers often become blind to their own typographical and logical errors
options.C: Colleagues are legally required to rewrite the entire document for you
options.D: Peer review replaces the need for a formal methodology section

explanation: When you've stared at a paper for hours, typos hide from you! A fresh pair of eyes can spot little mistakes in seconds.

question: What is the correct order of the three meningeal layers from the outside (near the skull) to the inside (touching the brain)?

options.A: Dura mater, arachnoid mater, pia mater
options.B: Pia mater, arachnoid mater, dura mater
options.C: Dura mater, pia mater, arachnoid mater
options.D: Arachnoid mater, dura mater, pia mater

explanation: Think of it like layers of clothing: the tough dura mater is your outer jacket, the web-like arachnoid is your sweater in the middle, and the delicate pia mater is your singlet hugging your skin!

question: As a nurse, how must you make sure the traction weights are positioned during your shift?

options.A: They are adjusted upward by the patient
options.B: They are hidden beneath heavy wool blankets
options.C: They rest securely on the foot of the bed
options.D: They hang freely without touching the floor

explanation: Always check those weights! If they touch the floor, they lose their pulling power and the therapy won't work.

question: A client refuses a specific birth control method due to local community rumors. What is the best nursing approach?

options.A: Refuse to provide any further healthcare services to the client
options.B: Listen respectfully and provide accurate education to clear up the rumors
options.C: Dismiss the client's worries as silly and push the method anyway
options.D: Tell the client that community opinions should never matter

explanation: Respectful listening combined with gentle, accurate education helps address fears rooted in social stigma and community misconceptions. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h2)

question: In a typical clinic or hospital, about how much of the total waste generated is ordinary non-hazardous general rubbish?

options.A: 50 to 60 percent
options.B: 75 to 90 percent
options.C: 10 to 25 percent
options.D: 95 to 99 percent

explanation: You'd be surprised! The vast majority of waste coming from wards is just ordinary paper, food wrappings, and packaging—leaving only a small fraction that needs special hazardous care.

question: What is the main goal of adding psychosocial support to post-abortion care?

options.A: To diagnose underlying psychiatric disorders through formal testing
options.B: To help patients process emotional distress, fear, and stigma
options.C: To convince patients to testify against unsafe abortion providers
options.D: To provide legal representation for women facing criminal charges

explanation: Spot on! Psychosocial support offers a safe, compassionate space to address the emotional trauma or guilt associated with pregnancy loss.

question: What happens inside the eye of a person with cataracts?

options.A: The natural lens becomes cloudy and blocks clear light
options.B: The macula breaks down and destroys central vision
options.C: Intraocular pressure rises and damages the optic nerve
options.D: Tiny blood vessels on the retina burst and bleed

explanation: Cataracts are characterized by the opacification or clouding of the eye's natural lens, which blurs the incoming light. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h2)

question: What best defines an accident in community health terms?

options.A: A planned medical procedure with complications
options.B: A chronic disease with a slow onset
options.C: An unexpected event causing injury or harm
options.D: An unavoidable natural health disaster

explanation: Accidents are sudden, unexpected events that cause physical harm or damage to individuals. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h1)

question: Why might a patient on a ventilator for a long time be switched from an ordinary breathing tube (endotracheal tube) to a tracheostomy?

options.A: To completely eliminate the risk of respiratory infections
options.B: To reduce damage to the vocal cords and larynx
options.C: To allow the patient to swallow solid food immediately
options.D: To make the ventilator machine run faster

explanation: Endotracheal tubes passing through the mouth can hurt the vocal cords over time. Moving to a tracheostomy protects the larynx during long-term care.

question: Why do nurses and therapists break big tasks like bathing into smaller, simple steps for neurological clients?

options.A: To keep the client sitting quietly in a chair for hours at a time
options.B: To ensure the nursing staff finishes their shift work much faster
options.C: To prevent the client from ever using any assistive technology
options.D: To reduce cognitive overload and encourage successful task completion

explanation: Big tasks can feel overwhelming to a healing brain. Breaking them down builds confidence, stops frustration, and lets the client win step by step!

question: What is a primary benefit of addressing workplace conflicts early in a clinical setting?

options.A: It prevents small disagreements from turning into a toxic atmosphere
options.B: It removes the need for shift handovers and team meetings
options.C: It stops doctors from ever questioning nursing care plans
options.D: It guarantees that nurses receive an immediate salary increase

explanation: Correct! Addressing issues early keeps the ward vibe positive and ensures patient safety stays front and center.

question: A nurse sorts patients by their blood groups (A, B, AB, or O). What level of measurement is this?

options.A: Ratio
options.B: Ordinal
options.C: Nominal
options.D: Interval

explanation: Spot on! Blood groups are just names or categories with no numerical value or rank. Whenever you're just labeling categories, it's nominal data.

question: How do strong social support systems help protect a person's mental health?

options.A: They eliminate all stressful events from happening in life
options.B: They ensure the person never experiences sadness
options.C: They replace the need for professional psychiatric medication
options.D: They provide emotional validation and practical help during crises

explanation: Having friends or family who listen and stand by you makes heavy burdens feel much lighter.

question: Which vitamin supplement is routinely given to pregnant mothers to prevent neural tube defects?

options.A: Folic acid
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Iron

explanation: Spot on! Folic acid is vital for early cell division and helps prevent serious birth defects of the brain and spine.

question: Why should patients with a pacemaker avoid contact sports?

options.A: High impact activities cause the heart rate to become permanently fixed
options.B: Rapid arm movements will completely drain the battery within a few hours
options.C: Physical blows to the chest can damage the generator or dislodge the wires
options.D: Sweating during heavy exercise will rust the titanium case of the battery

explanation: Hard blows to the chest can break the wires or shift the device out of place. Protecting that pocket is key!

question: Why does an emergency cesarean delivery carry a higher infection risk than a planned vaginal birth?

options.A: Patients undergoing cesarean birth never receive prophylactic antibiotics
options.B: Surgical incision exposes internal tissues and prior labor introduces bacteria
options.C: Suturing techniques used in emergency surgery always trap skin flora
options.D: The sterile operating theatre environment promotes bacterial growth

explanation: An abdominal surgery creates a fresh wound, and if the mother was already in labor with ruptured membranes, bacteria may have already entered the lower reproductive tract.

question: What is the primary point of entry for individuals into the national health system?

options.A: Private specialist clinic
options.B: Primary Health Care
options.C: National health ministry
options.D: Tertiary teaching hospital

explanation: Primary Health Care serves as the first level of contact for individuals and families entering the health system. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is the name of the upper opening into the true pelvis?

options.A: Acetabulum
options.B: Pelvic inlet
options.C: Pelvic outlet
options.D: Greater sciatic notch

explanation: You're doing great! The pelvic inlet is literally the 'entrance' or upper opening where the baby first enters the true pelvis.

question: What crucial advice should you give a patient prescribed a course of antibiotics?

options.A: Complete the entire course even if symptoms disappear early
options.B: Stop taking the pills immediately when fever subsides
options.C: Double the next dose if you forget to take one on time
options.D: Share leftover medicine with family members who feel sick

explanation: Always finish the prescription! Stopping early lets the strongest bacteria survive and bounce back stronger than before.

question: You just finished soaking and washing your patient's hands. What is the most important thing to do before picking up the clippers?

options.A: Applying thick scented lotion to the skin
options.B: Pushing the cuticles back with force
options.C: Drying the hands and fingers thoroughly
options.D: Massaging the palms to improve circulation

explanation: Exactly! Wet hands make the clippers slippery, and trapped moisture can cause issues. Always dry them well first!

question: What common blood collection mistake can make a patient's potassium level look falsely high on a lab report?

options.A: Hemolysis of the blood sample
options.B: Using a small gauge needle for a deep vein
options.C: Leaving the tourniquet on for too short a time
options.D: Storing the sample inside a warm incubator

explanation: Spot on! If red blood cells break open (hemolyze) during a rough blood draw, they spill their inner potassium into the sample, giving a fake high reading.

question: How does pelvic floor physical therapy help treat genito-pelvic pain?

options.A: It removes scar tissue from previous vaginal surgeries
options.B: It permanently blocks nerve signals to the clitoris
options.C: It increases systemic testosterone production instantly
options.D: It relaxes and conditions hypertonic pelvic muscles

explanation: Spot on! When pelvic muscles are overworked and too tight (hypertonic), physical therapy teaches the patient how to consciously relax and lengthen them.

question: At what exact times do we check a newborn's Apgar score?

options.A: Immediately at birth and 30 minutes later
options.B: 1 minute and 5 minutes after birth
options.C: 10 minutes and 20 minutes after birth
options.D: 5 minutes and 10 minutes after birth

explanation: We do Apgar at 1 minute to see how the baby handled birth, and at 5 minutes to see how they are adjusting to the big wide world outside!

question: Who benefits the most when a community achieves herd immunity?

options.A: Patients recovering from surgical procedures
options.B: Only individuals with strong innate immunity
options.C: Vulnerable people who cannot receive vaccines
options.D: Only adults who travel to other countries

explanation: Spot on! Herd immunity builds a protective ring around fragile individuals who cannot take vaccines themselves.

question: You review assessment data showing severe food insecurity, low body weight, and vitamin deficiency signs. What should you do next?

options.A: Focus only on recording daily fluid intake and ignore the social findings
options.B: Collaborate to create a practical care plan including dietary counseling and social support referrals
options.C: Order expensive invasive biopsies to confirm cellular micronutrient levels
options.D: Discharge the client immediately since nutritional deficits resolve without intervention

explanation: Since the issues involve both food and social hardship, your care plan needs to tackle both sides with counseling and support referrals.

question: How does aging infrastructure increase the risk of a human-made disaster?

options.A: It increases the likelihood of sudden structural collapse or utility failure
options.B: It stops human error from ever occurring in a workplace setting
options.C: It reduces the need for regulatory oversight and safety inspections
options.D: It guarantees that all industrial accidents will be prevented automatically

explanation: Exactly! Old, poorly maintained bridges, pipes, and wiring break down much easier when put under normal daily stress.

question: Which of these is a major barrier to using research in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Patients demanding that nurses read journals daily
options.B: An excess of free time available to clinical nurses
options.C: Too many research articles published in local languages
options.D: Lack of basic equipment and heavy staff workloads

explanation: So true! When the ward is packed and basic tools are short, it becomes tough to find the breathing room to test brand new research ideas.

question: What is an important nursing task to do right after a patient finishes eating to lower their risk of pneumonia?

options.A: Encouraging immediate strenuous walking
options.B: Lowering the head of the bed completely
options.C: Offering a large glass of thin water
options.D: Providing thorough oral hygiene

explanation: Brushing the teeth and cleaning the mouth clears away leftover food bits and bacteria that could otherwise slip into the lungs later.

question: How do nitrate medications help stop chest pain?

options.A: By speeding up the electrical rhythm of the heart
options.B: By dilating blood vessels to reduce heart workload
options.C: By thickening the blood to improve clot formation
options.D: By increasing the heart rate to pump faster

explanation: Nitrates act like widening the road—they relax blood vessels so blood flows more easily, taking a huge load off the heart and easing the pain.

question: Which drug class is commonly used to help with burning or shooting nerve pain?

options.A: Antacids
options.B: Blood thinners
options.C: Anticonvulsants
options.D: Loop diuretics

explanation: Anticonvulsants (normally used for seizures) calm down jittery, overactive nerves that cause sharp, burning nerve pain.

question: Which physical sign is a reliable indicator that vital organs are getting enough blood flow?

options.A: Dry and cracked lips
options.B: Adequate urine output
options.C: Slow and deep breathing
options.D: Cold and pale fingers

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! Good urine output tells you the kidneys are well-perfused, meaning the heart and blood vessels are keeping good pressure up.

question: Which type of scale is best suited for an adult patient who is completely unable to stand?

options.A: A specialized chair or bed scale
options.B: A standard beam balance scale
options.C: A hanging infant spring scale
options.D: A flat digital floor scale

explanation: Chair and bed scales allow nurses to obtain accurate weights for immobile patients without forcing them to stand. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why is teamwork between different healthcare pros so important in home nutrition care?

options.A: Doctors require every single discipline to sign off on grocery lists
options.B: It ensures the nurse does not have to visit the patient's home very often
options.C: It prevents family members from participating in meal preparation
options.D: Different specialists bring unique skills like swallowing therapy or diet design to keep the patient safe

explanation: Spot on! Speech therapists handle swallowing, dietitians handle meal plans, and together they keep the patient safe.

question: What usually causes Transfusion-Associated Circulatory Overload (TACO)?

options.A: A mismatched ABO blood type between donor and recipient
options.B: Bacterial contamination of the red blood cells during storage
options.C: An allergic response to donor plasma proteins in the blood bag
options.D: Infusing blood too rapidly for the patient's cardiovascular system to handle

explanation: TACO happens when fluid goes in faster than a patient's heart can pump it, causing fluid backup in the lungs.

question: Through which bone does smell nerve fibers pass to reach the brain?

options.A: Internal acoustic meatus of the temporal bone
options.B: Superior orbital fissure of the orbit
options.C: Cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone
options.D: Foramen magnum of the occipital bone

explanation: Spot on! Tiny nerve fibers pass upward through the tiny holes in the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone to reach the brain's olfactory bulb. Fun anatomy fact to keep in mind!

question: A patient has Type A blood. What type of antibodies circulate in their plasma?

options.A: No antibodies at all
options.B: Anti-A antibodies
options.C: Anti-B antibodies
options.D: Both anti-A and anti-B antibodies

explanation: People with Type A blood have A antigens on their cells, so their immune system develops anti-B antibodies to fight off foreign B-type blood. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why is it important for nurses to study both morbidity and mortality statistics together?

options.A: To prove that nobody gets sick in rural areas
options.B: To replace the need for physical patient examinations
options.C: To see which illnesses cause suffering versus which ones cause death
options.D: To calculate the exact salary of medical doctors

explanation: Looking at both illness rates and death rates provides a complete picture of the total health burden affecting a population. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why is it important to move mental health care beyond hospital walls into communities?

options.A: Because doctors prefer working outdoors with crowds
options.B: Because hospitals are too expensive to clean
options.C: Because community members can replace trained psychiatrists entirely
options.D: Because daily social roots and support systems heavily influence well-being

explanation: Mental health is deeply connected to a person's everyday environment, making local community support essential for lasting recovery and prevention. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h1)

question: A patient with severe nephrotic syndrome is most likely to report which initial pattern of swelling?

options.A: Severe swelling limited to the toes
options.B: Sudden swelling of only the right hand
options.C: Puffiness around the eyes upon waking up
options.D: Throbbing pain and swelling in the jaw

explanation: Periorbital edema is a classic early sign of fluid shifting into loose facial tissues overnight while the patient is lying flat. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the main reason why hospitals and wards have policies?

options.A: To direct daily clinical actions and standardize care
options.B: To replace formal nursing education and training
options.C: To reduce the number of employed nurses in a unit
options.D: To increase the cost of purchasing medical supplies

explanation: Policies give us clear, step-by-step guidance so every nurse delivers safe, consistent care. Think of them as your reliable roadmap on the ward!

question: Why might a nurse choose group counselling over individual counselling for a diabetes education program?

options.A: It allows the nurse to give private, confidential medical diagnoses
options.B: It reaches multiple patients at once and encourages shared learning
options.C: It is the only legal method to teach carbohydrate counting
options.D: It completely prevents patients from asking questions about food

explanation: Groups are efficient for widespread conditions like diabetes, saving time while building a supportive community spirit. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h3)

question: What physical movement inside the heart makes the first heart sound (the 'lub')?

options.A: The atrioventricular valves slamming shut
options.B: Blood rushing into the main veins
options.C: The left atrium wall squeezing
options.D: The semilunar valves opening up

explanation: That familiar 'lub-dub' sound is actually just doors shutting! The first sound is the AV valves snapping closed so blood doesn't flow backward.

question: When someone pushes back against your advocacy campaign, which of these should you NOT do?

options.A: Dismissing the critic's concerns as foolish and uneducated
options.B: Anticipating counter-arguments ahead of time with solid data
options.C: Acknowledging their point of view respectfully before pivoting
options.D: Remaining calm, professional, and prepared with evidence

explanation: Never insult or dismiss your critics! Staying respectful keeps your credibility high, even when people disagree with you.

question: What does 'food security' mean for a population?

options.A: Storing a ten-year supply of grains in underground bunkers
options.B: Having military protection around every food warehouse
options.C: Constant physical, social, and economic access to safe and enough food
options.D: Producing every single food item inside the country's borders

explanation: Food security simply means everyone has reliable access to enough safe, nutritious food to live a healthy life.

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary in palliative care?

options.A: To reduce the number of working hours for individual doctors
options.B: Because physical, emotional, and social needs require diverse expert skills
options.C: To ensure that family members never have to help at home
options.D: Because hospital regulations legally mandate large staffing numbers

explanation: It takes a village! Since a serious illness affects the body, mind, and soul, we need different experts—doctors, nurses, social workers, and chaplains—working as a team.

question: Why do we have a postnatal referral system in place?

options.A: To reduce the total number of patients visiting government hospitals
options.B: To connect primary clinics with facilities that can handle emergencies
options.C: To collect data for national health research and statistics
options.D: To provide routine immunization schedules for newborns

explanation: Think of a referral system as a bridge! It links small community health posts to advanced hospitals so mothers and babies get rapid help when an emergency hits.

question: Which delivery method is most frequently associated with physical trauma to the foetal skull?

options.A: Spontaneous vertex delivery
options.B: Water birth delivery
options.C: Instrument-assisted delivery
options.D: Elective caesarean section

explanation: The mechanical forces applied by forceps or vacuum extractors place the newborn at a much higher risk of skull and scalp injuries. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h2)

question: What is the final organ responsible for turning vitamin D into its active hormonal form, calcitriol?

options.A: Stomach
options.B: Liver
options.C: Skin
options.D: Kidneys

explanation: The kidneys perform the final activation step on vitamin D so the body can properly absorb calcium. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which major international conference linked population policy directly with human rights?

options.A: The Geneva Convention on the Treatment of Patients
options.B: The Alma-Ata Declaration on Primary Health Care
options.C: The 1994 International Conference on Population and Development in Cairo
options.D: The 1995 World Conference on Women held in Beijing

explanation: It's the 1994 Cairo Conference! This was a massive turning point that shifted global health focus toward empowering individuals and protecting their rights.

question: Why don't doctors do throat swabs for every person who walks in with a mild cold?

options.A: Most common colds are viral and resolve with supportive care
options.B: Laboratory tests are completely inaccurate for respiratory illnesses
options.C: Testing always causes severe physical trauma to the throat
options.D: Viral infections require immediate intravenous antibiotics

explanation: Exactly! Since normal colds are viral and clear up on their own, testing and antibiotics aren't needed—just rest and fluids.

question: Which action best supports the emotional needs of a patient newly diagnosed with a blood disorder?

options.A: Leaving educational brochures on the bedside table and leaving
options.B: Providing active listening and validating their concerns
options.C: Directing all emotional questions strictly to the attending physician
options.D: Telling them not to worry because things could be worse

explanation: A new diagnosis is scary. Listening with empathy and validating their feelings builds trust and helps them cope better.

question: What is a major safety concern when giving sleeping pills (sedative-hypnotics) to older adults?

options.A: Severe respiratory alkalosis
options.B: Hypertensive crisis
options.C: Permanent hearing loss
options.D: Increased risk of falls

explanation: Sleeping pills can cause daytime drowsiness and dizziness, making older adults unsteady on their feet and putting them at a high risk for accidental falls.

question: Why should nurses avoid using heavy medical jargon when teaching community members?

options.A: Patients will lose respect for a nurse who speaks too plainly
options.B: Using simple words takes longer than using advanced scientific terms
options.C: Complex medical terms confuse listeners and hinder clear understanding
options.D: Medical words are copyrighted and illegal to speak in public places

explanation: Exactly! Speaking in simple, everyday language ensures your audience truly understands what you are saying and what actions to take.

question: How can poverty make health education harder to put into practice?

options.A: It automatically cures all infectious diseases
options.B: Patients may struggle to afford recommended foods or medications
options.C: It prevents community members from gathering together
options.D: It stops nurses from speaking local languages

explanation: Financial hardship makes it tough for patients to follow health advice that requires buying prescribed drugs or specific nutritious foods.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do for a patient going into shock from severe post-abortion bleeding?

options.A: Perform a detailed psychosocial history regarding the pregnancy
options.B: Send the patient immediately for diagnostic pelvic ultrasound
options.C: Administer oral rehydration salts and counsel on contraception
options.D: Insert large-bore intravenous lines for fluid resuscitation

explanation: ABC comes first—and in bleeding shock, getting IV lines open fast to pump fluids and restore blood volume is an absolute lifesaver! You've got this.

question: What is usually the very first sign that a Guinea worm is ready to come out?

options.A: A widespread rash over the entire chest and back
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin
options.C: A painful skin blister with a burning sensation
options.D: Painless swelling of the finger joints

explanation: You got it! Patients feel a sharp, burning pain right where the blister pops up before the worm emerges. Great clinical observation skills!

question: About how soon after a long bone fracture should a nurse watch out for fat embolism syndrome?

options.A: Immediately within the first ten minutes
options.B: Twenty-four to seventy-two hours
options.C: Several months during late healing
options.D: Two to three weeks

explanation: Fat droplets take a little time to travel from the bone marrow into the bloodstream. Keep your eyes peeled during the first 1 to 3 days after a long bone break!

question: A nursing mother complains of painful swelling and redness in only her left calf. What should you do?

options.A: Advise her to apply hot compresses and stay in bed for three days
options.B: Prescribe oral iron supplements for suspected postpartum anaemia
options.C: Reassure her that this is a normal muscular strain from carrying the baby
options.D: Refer her urgently for suspected deep vein thrombosis

explanation: Pain and swelling in just one leg is a warning sign of a blood clot (DVT). It needs an urgent hospital check to keep her safe!

question: Why are strong people skills even more important in community nursing than in a big hospital?

options.A: Hospital nurses do not need to communicate with patients and families.
options.B: Patients in communities are more likely to reject care if they feel judged or misunderstood.
options.C: Community nurses rarely perform physical assessments or give medications.
options.D: Community settings have unlimited funding for medical technology.

explanation: Spot on! Since you are visiting people in their own private space, building a warm connection means everything. If they feel judged, they simply won't let you help.

question: Why are secondary complications so dangerous for patients with brain or nerve injuries?

options.A: They can worsen the initial injury and cause further damage
options.B: They disappear without any medical intervention
options.C: They always reverse the effects of the primary disease
options.D: They only affect the peripheral nervous system

explanation: Secondary problems put extra stress on a body that is already struggling, often leading to a much worse outcome than the original injury. You've got this!

question: What physical signs are most typical of an acute gout flare in a joint?

options.A: Slow, painless swelling that develops over several months
options.B: Intense redness, extreme tenderness, and localized heat
options.C: Visible shortening of the limb and muscle atrophy
options.D: Cool, pale skin with complete numbness and no pain

explanation: When gout flares up, the joint gets super angry—it turns bright red, feels very hot to the touch, and hurts so much you can barely let anyone look at it.

question: A nurse notices that new mothers in the postnatal ward look anxious about breastfeeding. Which option turns this into a well-focused research study?

options.A: Asking every nurse on the ward how they feel about their personal jobs
options.B: Reviewing the financial cost of building a new maternity ward
options.C: Studying why the entire healthcare system in the country is failing mothers
options.D: Evaluating whether a peer support group lowers anxiety scores among first-time breastfeeding mothers

explanation: Spot on! This takes a real ward observation (breastfeeding anxiety) and turns it into a clear, measurable plan with a specific group of people.

question: A patient arrives gaspering for air, coughing up pink, frothy sputum, and with wet crackles in their chest. What is the best immediate medical order to anticipate?

options.A: Administering intravenous furosemide
options.B: Instructing the patient to perform deep breathing exercises
options.C: Starting oral iron supplementation
options.D: Collecting a 24-hour urine sample

explanation: Frothy sputum and crackles scream fluid overload (heart failure). Diuretics like furosemide help pull that fluid off quickly so they can breathe.

question: What factor has the greatest influence on peripheral vascular resistance?

options.A: Total vessel length
options.B: Overall body height
options.C: Vessel radius
options.D: Red blood cell count

explanation: Small changes in vessel radius create exponential changes in resistance, making constriction and dilation the primary way the body controls blood pressure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the main reason a researcher tries to control variables in a study?

options.A: To ensure patients never experience any side effects
options.B: To make the research process as fast as possible
options.C: To isolate the specific effect of the intervention being tested
options.D: To hide unwanted data from the final report

explanation: Brilliant! Controlling variables helps you say for sure: 'Yes, this specific drug or nursing action is what made the patient better.'

question: In infection control, what do we mean by a 'reservoir'?

options.A: The natural home where a microorganism lives and multiplies
options.B: The method by which a germ travels through the air
options.C: An opening where germs leave the human body
options.D: A person who is vulnerable to catching a disease

explanation: Think of a reservoir as a cozy hangout spot for germs—it could be a human, an animal, soil, or even equipment where they live and grow.

question: Which of the following is a common systemic challenge faced by maternal care teams in low-resource settings?

options.A: Mandatory retirement for midwives at age thirty
options.B: Zero workload and extremely short working hours
options.C: Staff shortages and lack of functional equipment
options.D: An excessive surplus of modern diagnostic machines

explanation: In many under-resourced settings, frontline health workers battle daily with personnel deficits and broken equipment. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h8)

question: Why do we track wastage rates on our monthly injection safety form?

options.A: It automatically increases the monthly government drug allocation
options.B: It helps managers justify future procurement requests and reduce loss
options.C: It replaces the need for keeping a physical pharmacy inventory
options.D: It punishes nurses who accidentally drop sterile items

explanation: Spot on! Tracking broken or wasted items shows management where supplies are leaking, helping us order better next time.

question: In which of these situations is giving a strong purgative UNSAFE?

options.A: When a patient has acute abdominal pain of unknown origin
options.B: When a patient needs to avoid straining after childbirth
options.C: When managing mild constipation caused by dietary changes
options.D: When preparing an adult patient for a scheduled colonoscopy

explanation: Never guess with belly pain! Unexplained pain could mean appendicitis or a blockage—giving a purgative here can be disastrous.

question: Which tool has become a standard digital replacement for paper patient charts in modern healthcare facilities?

options.A: Printed pocket notebooks
options.B: Electronic health records
options.C: Manual bedside blackboards
options.D: Audio cassette recordings

explanation: Electronic health records allow fast, secure sharing of patient data across interprofessional healthcare teams. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h6)

question: A patient comes in with sharp, cramping side pain and a history of passing tiny gravel in their urine. What is the doctor most likely looking for with an IVP?

options.A: An acute urinary tract infection
options.B: Renal calculi or kidney stones
options.C: Glomerular nephritis
options.D: Benign prostatic hyperplasia

explanation: Spot on! That sharp flank pain combined with gravel in the urine is the classic sign of kidney stones (renal calculi) hiding in the tract.

question: Which behavior is typical in a patient with Korsakoff syndrome?

options.A: Confabulation, where they make up stories to fill memory gaps
options.B: Uncontrollable shaking of both hands while eating
options.C: Throwing angry tantrums at family members
options.D: Being completely mute and refusing to talk to anyone

explanation: Spot on! Patients with Korsakoff often unconsciously invent details (confabulate) to cover up the blank spots in their memory.

question: What happens to extra glucose when your body already has enough energy?

options.A: It is stored in the liver and muscles as glycogen
options.B: It is turned into red blood cells in the spleen
options.C: It is immediately converted into bone marrow cells
options.D: It is excreted entirely through the sweat glands

explanation: When there's extra sugar around, the body packs it neatly away in the liver and muscles as glycogen for later use. Smart storage!

question: What do we call the complete group of people that a researcher is interested in studying?

options.A: Pilot cohort
options.B: Target population
options.C: Control group
options.D: Sample subset

explanation: The target population is the big group that shares the exact traits you want to investigate—like all nursing students in Nigeria, for instance!

question: Why do many young women in Nigeria turn to secret, unsafe abortion methods?

options.A: Advise from community health extension workers
options.B: Preference for traditional herbal preparations over modern medicine
options.C: Fear of social stigma and strict legal or religious restrictions
options.D: Lack of awareness that government hospitals offer free services

explanation: Societal pressure, shame, and strict laws often push frightened individuals away from safe hospitals and into risky, hidden places. A supportive nurse makes all the difference!

question: Why should you always teach your patients the difference between a normal side effect and a dangerous adverse reaction?

options.A: It prevents panic over normal symptoms while ensuring prompt reporting of dangerous signs
options.B: It eliminates the need for any follow-up visits with the primary doctor
options.C: It guarantees the patient will never experience any drug discomfort
options.D: It allows the patient to legally prescribe their own antidote medications

explanation: Mild drowsiness is okay, but throat swelling is an emergency! Teaching the difference keeps patients calm and safe.

question: What do we mean by 'socioeconomic determinants of health'?

options.A: Blood pressure readings taken at annual checkups
options.B: Income level, education, and living conditions
options.C: The specific surgical tools used in major hospitals
options.D: Genetic mutations inherited from biological parents

explanation: These are the social and money-related factors—like how much money you make, where you live, and your education—that heavily shape your health.

question: What happens to the body during activation of the sympathetic nervous system?

options.A: Digestion speeds up to process recent meals
options.B: Heart rate increases and airways dilate for quick action
options.C: Pupils constrict to focus on close objects
options.D: Blood flow is directed entirely to the stomach

explanation: The sympathetic division prepares the body for stressful or emergency situations by boosting alertness and physical readiness. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h4)

question: During normal internal rotation, which way does the back of the baby's head (occiput) usually turn?

options.A: Toward the maternal pubic symphysis
options.B: Toward the hollow of the sacrum
options.C: Toward the right lateral pelvic wall
options.D: Toward the left maternal iliac crest

explanation: Spot on! The occiput rotates forward toward the pubic bone so it can easily slip out of the birth canal.

question: Why do nurses inject a little bit of air into a closed medication vial before pulling out the liquid?

options.A: To increase the potency of the drug
options.B: To mix the medication with sterile gas
options.C: To prevent a vacuum and ease withdrawal
options.D: To sterilize the rubber stopper surface

explanation: Vials are sealed tight. If you don't pump a little air in first, you end up fighting a vacuum trying to pull the liquid out. Air creates pressure that makes drawing the med smooth and easy!

question: Why might a nurse face pushback when trying to bring about changes in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Government laws strictly forbid nurses from speaking in public
options.B: Patients always oppose changes that improve their health outcomes
options.C: Medical doctors are legally required to stop all nursing activities
options.D: Superiors may feel threatened or prefer to maintain corrupt or comfortable habits

explanation: You nailed it! People in charge sometimes resist change because they are used to old habits or feel exposed when a nurse points out system failures.

question: When you wash your hands thoroughly, which part of the chain of infection are you directly blocking?

options.A: Mode of transmission
options.B: Infectious reservoir
options.C: Portal of entry
options.D: Susceptible host

explanation: Exactly! Handwashing washes away germs before they can hitch a ride from one surface or patient to another.

question: What is the minimum recommended fasting time before a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: 24 hours
options.B: 4 hours
options.C: 8 hours
options.D: 2 hours

explanation: A minimum of 8 hours without caloric intake is required to ensure the digestive system is at rest and baseline glucose can be measured. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h4)

question: Which of the following is a common sign of compassion fatigue in a nurse?

options.A: A sudden increase in clinical documentation speed
options.B: Excitement and eagerness to take on extra overtime hours
options.C: Increased physical strength and boundless energy on every shift
options.D: Emotional exhaustion and a feeling of numbness toward patients

explanation: Compassion fatigue often manifests as emotional weariness, numbness, and exhaustion from caring for suffering individuals over time. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h8)

question: A patient experiences a sudden drop in heart rate and active digestion after eating a large meal. Which system is most active?

options.A: Central sensory system
options.B: Parasympathetic nervous system
options.C: Somatic motor system
options.D: Sympathetic nervous system

explanation: The parasympathetic division dominates during restful states, encouraging digestion and slowing down bodily activity. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why must a community health nurse pay special attention to vulnerable groups during an assessment?

options.A: They often lack the voice or resources to access care on their own
options.B: They pay higher taxes to support the local primary health center
options.C: They make up the majority of the staff working in the hospitals
options.D: They are the only people in the community who ever get sick

explanation: Because these groups often suffer quietly without demanding services, it's our duty as nurses to actively find them and be their advocates.

question: What is the coolest superpower of adaptive immunity compared to innate immunity?

options.A: It relies entirely on physical skin barriers to keep germs out
options.B: It creates immunological memory for faster responses to repeat infections
options.C: It provides instant protection within minutes of touching a pathogen
options.D: It does not require white blood cells to eliminate foreign microbes

explanation: Adaptive immunity never forgets a face! It remembers specific germs it has fought before, so if the same germ shows up again, it attacks much faster and stronger.

question: Why is a urinary catheter put in place during emergency care for severe abortion complications?

options.A: To flush the bladder with antiseptics to kill germs
options.B: To keep the patient from moving around the ward
options.C: To monitor hourly urine output and check kidney function
options.D: To collect a clean urine sample for a routine pregnancy test

explanation: Watching urine output closely tells us if the kidneys are getting enough blood flow while recovering from shock. Excellent clinical tracking!

question: Why must a patient taking the blood thinner warfarin watch how many leafy green vegetables they eat?

options.A: The food inhibits liver enzymes and causes fatal bleeding episodes
options.B: The food counteracts the blood-thinning effect, risking clot formation
options.C: The food binds to the drug in the stomach and stops absorption
options.D: The food lowers blood pressure and causes sudden fainting spells

explanation: Leafy greens are loaded with Vitamin K, which naturally helps blood clot. Since Vitamin K fights against warfarin's job, sudden changes in diet can put the patient at risk.

question: Why are human reservoirs (like people carrying a germ) harder to track than stationary things like soil?

options.A: Environmental spores cannot be detected by modern laboratory testing
options.B: Infected humans can move freely and spread pathogens before showing symptoms
options.C: Human carriers are completely immune to all forms of standard medical treatment
options.D: Soil bacteria can replicate much faster than any human viral pathogen

explanation: Unlike a patch of soil, people walk around, travel, and mingle—often feeling completely fine while carrying germs. That's what makes human carriers so tricky to spot!

question: Which official council regulates the practice and licensing of midwives in Nigeria?

options.A: West African Health Community Board
options.B: National Union of Local Government Employees
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: Medical and Dental Association of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the body that sets our professional standards, trains us, and gives us our licenses to practice safely.

question: Which sign tells you an eye infection is likely bacterial rather than viral?

options.A: Clear, watery fluid production
options.B: Severe itching in both eyes
options.C: Complete loss of central vision
options.D: Thick, pus-like eye discharge

explanation: Bacterial eye infections love to produce thick, sticky pus (purulent drainage) that often glues the eyelids shut while sleeping.

question: Which environmental factor constantly threatens medical electronics on a boat?

options.A: Excessive exposure to underground soil
options.B: Complete absence of magnetic fields
options.C: Saltwater corrosion and high humidity
options.D: Constant freezing temperatures indoors

explanation: Correct! The salty, humid sea air can easily rust and ruin medical devices, so nurses have to maintain equipment with extra care.

question: Which of these items counts as pathological waste?

options.A: Surgical gauze soaked in blood
options.B: An empty plastic intravenous fluid bag
options.C: A surgically removed human gallbladder
options.D: A used hypodermic needle and syringe

explanation: Pathological waste refers to body parts, tissues, or organs removed during surgery or autopsies. Neat to know for clinical sorting!
