question: What is the quickest and most practical way for a nurse to check what a patient has eaten recently during a busy clinic day?

options.A: Admitting the patient for a week
options.B: Testing stool samples for fat
options.C: Asking for a 24-hour dietary recall
options.D: Ordering a full metabolic blood panel

explanation: Spot on! Asking 'What did you eat and drink yesterday?' gives you a fast, reliable picture of their current intake.

question: What should a nurse do if a sound-minded patient at home refuses treatment?

options.A: Respect the refusal and document the discussion thoroughly
options.B: Call the police to arrest the family members
options.C: Force the patient to take the treatment immediately
options.D: Ignore the refusal and administer the drug secretly

explanation: Exactly right! Competent patients have every right to decide what happens to their bodies, including saying no to treatment.

question: A local government wants nurses to happily stay long-term in remote health posts. Which step is most effective?

options.A: Reducing the operational hours of remote clinics to twice a week
options.B: Threatening to dismiss any nurse who requests a transfer to an urban center
options.C: Eliminating all training programs to keep staff working on site full-time
options.D: Providing staff quarters, hardship allowances, and regular promotion opportunities

explanation: Taking care of staff needs—like providing a place to live and rewarding their hard work—makes them want to stay and serve the community.

question: How can a new home care agency best protect its nurses from safety risks when visiting unfamiliar areas?

options.A: Instructing nurses to never document any clinical findings
options.B: Stopping all home visits after morning hours
options.C: Vetting client locations and utilizing tracking or communication tools
options.D: Requiring families to purchase expensive hospital equipment

explanation: Brilliant! Checking locations beforehand and using check-in tools helps keep field nurses safe and secure.

question: What does 'segregation of duties' mean when managing DRF cash?

options.A: Different people should handle drug dispensing and cash collection
options.B: Auditors must check the pharmacy books once every year
options.C: Suppliers must deliver drugs before payment is approved
options.D: Pharmacists must work morning and night shifts alternately

explanation: Exactly! When one person hands out drugs and another person collects the money, it creates a checks-and-balances system that prevents theft and keeps everyone honest.

question: In which year was the historic Alma-Ata Declaration on Primary Health Care held?
explanation: The landmark international conference that shaped modern community nursing took place in Alma-Ata in 1978. Great to keep in mind for your exams!

question: What is the main role of peer educators in youth-friendly health programs?

options.A: Performing minor surgical procedures in community schools
options.B: Bridging the gap by sharing health info and encouraging clinic visits
options.C: Enforcing hospital rules on visiting adult patients
options.D: Managing the financial accounts of the local hospital

explanation: Teens trust their peers! Peer educators are fantastic at spreading positive health habits and helping friends feel safe visiting the clinic.

question: Why is spotting patient risks early considered a protective action?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will never experience an infection
options.B: It allows nurses to build barriers against potential hazards
options.C: It removes all clinical responsibilities from the doctor
options.D: It stops patients from moving around the ward

explanation: Spotting risks beforehand lets you put preventative steps in place before an accident or complication actually happens. You've got this!

question: What happens in our lungs when we breathe in irritating particles?

options.A: White blood cells are recruited, leading to inflammation and mucus production
options.B: Air sacs expand permanently and never deflate again
options.C: Blood flow to the lungs stops completely to protect the heart
options.D: The lung tissue instantly becomes immune to all future infections

explanation: Great! When irritants enter, our immune system steps in, causing swelling and extra mucus, which makes breathing a bit tougher.

question: When cancer treatment cannot cure the disease, but aims to stop tumor growth and extend life, what is this main goal called?

options.A: Palliation
options.B: Cure
options.C: Prevention
options.D: Control

explanation: You've got this! When complete cure isn't possible, 'control' is the goal—stopping the cancer from spreading further to help the patient live a longer, fuller life.

question: Which symptom is a classic warning sign of severely high blood pressure?

options.A: Painful swelling of the ankle joints
options.B: Sudden uncontrollable shivering
options.C: Severe yellowing of the skin
options.D: Early morning occipital headache

explanation: Correct! A throbbing headache at the back of the head, especially right when waking up, is a classic sign of very high blood pressure.

question: A patient's blood pressure drops dangerously low after heavy bleeding. Which nursing action shows you are thinking about the whole body?

options.A: Telling the patient that other body organs are completely unaffected
options.B: Focusing solely on applying a bandage to the bleeding wound
options.C: Giving a sleeping pill to help the patient rest through the stress
options.D: Checking urine output because low blood pressure affects kidney function

explanation: Brilliant! Good nursing means remembering that blood loss reduces blood flow to vital organs like the kidneys, which immediately shows up in their urine output.

question: Which of these is a classic example of an environmental community risk?

options.A: A sudden outbreak of a viral infection
options.B: A high rate of unemployment among youths
options.C: Contaminated drinking water sources
options.D: Widespread cultural beliefs against vaccination

explanation: Bad water is a physical hazard right in the environment. It directly threatens everyone sharing that water source!

question: Which of these is a very common complaint from patients suffering from Long COVID?

options.A: Permanent darkening of the skin
options.B: Chronic fatigue and brain fog
options.C: Sudden bone fractures in the legs
options.D: Uncontrollable weight gain

explanation: You got it! Many people with Long COVID struggle with lingering tiredness and trouble concentrating, often called 'brain fog'.

question: During the dry season in northern Nigeria, a patient presents with a very stiff neck, high fever, and confusion. What should you suspect first?

options.A: Simple malaria fever
options.B: Cerebrospinal meningitis
options.C: Severe cholera infection
options.D: Typhoid fever illness

explanation: Spot on! A stiff neck and high fever are classic warning signs of meningitis, which tends to cause seasonal outbreaks in northern Nigeria during the dry season.

question: What does 'statistical power' mean in a research study?

options.A: The physical strength required by nurses to lift heavy patients
options.B: The total amount of funding secured for laboratory equipment
options.C: The ability of the study to detect a true effect if one exists
options.D: The speed at which data is entered into a computer spreadsheet

explanation: You got it! Power is basically your study's muscle—its ability to catch a real treatment difference if it's actually there.

question: A nurse sits down with local leaders and clinic staff to resolve a disagreement over immunization times. Which role is this nurse playing?

options.A: Patient
options.B: Prosecutor
options.C: Auditor
options.D: Mediator

explanation: You nailed it! A mediator steps in between two opposing sides to help them talk it out and find a peaceful, workable solution.

question: What is an important nursing check after a patient has an upper GI scope (endoscopy)?

options.A: Giving strong oral laxatives to clear out remaining dye
options.B: Putting warm compresses on the tummy every 15 minutes
options.C: Checking that the patient's gag reflex is back before giving food or water
options.D: Pushing the patient to eat a heavy meal right away to get their strength back

explanation: The throat spray numbs the back of the throat during the scope. If you feed them before the gag reflex returns, they could easily choke or aspirate.

question: How does a tracheostomy differ from an endotracheal tube?

options.A: An endotracheal tube is always permanent
options.B: A tracheostomy bypasses the upper airway via the neck
options.C: A tracheostomy goes through the mouth and nose
options.D: An endotracheal tube requires no mechanical support

explanation: Endotracheal tubes enter through the mouth or nose, whereas tracheostomy tubes enter directly through a surgical neck incision. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of an Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: To prevent patients from viewing their own medical test results
options.B: To store hospital financial budgets and staff work schedules
options.C: To replace traditional bedside nursing care with automated machines
options.D: To provide digital patient charts that can be shared across care settings

explanation: Spot on! EHRs put patient info into digital charts so healthcare teams can share accurate details safely across different departments. You've got this!

question: What is the main job of active vitamin D once processed by the kidneys?

options.A: To lower blood pressure by widening blood vessels
options.B: To speed up the filtration rate of the glomerulus
options.C: To stimulate red blood cell production in marrow
options.D: To promote calcium and phosphorus absorption in the gut

explanation: Spot on! Active vitamin D helps your intestines absorb calcium and phosphorus from your food so your body has what it needs for strong bones.

question: Why is rotating the application site essential when a patient uses transdermal patches?

options.A: To ensure the old patch stays stuck to the body for extra dosing
options.B: To prevent skin irritation, breakdown, and altered drug absorption
options.C: To force the medication to travel through different liver pathways
options.D: To stop the patient from forgetting where the patch was placed last week

explanation: Applying patches to the exact same spot repeatedly damages the skin barrier and can change how effectively the drug absorbs into the body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h8)

question: What is a major advantage of using lower individual drug doses in synergistic therapy?

options.A: It completely removes the need for nursing blood monitoring
options.B: It reduces the risk of toxic side effects for the patient
options.C: It allows patients to stop taking the drugs much sooner
options.D: It ensures the medication works instantly without absorption

explanation: Because the drugs boost each other, we can use smaller doses to get the job done, keeping the patient safer from harsh side effects.

question: What is the term for the variable that acts as the final measured outcome in a study?

options.A: Confounding variable
options.B: Dependent variable
options.C: Extraneous variable
options.D: Independent variable

explanation: You're doing great! The dependent variable is your final outcome that changes in response to what you tested.

question: Which of these is NOT a job of the ordinary sweat glands (eccrine glands)?

options.A: Excreting tiny amounts of body waste
options.B: Producing thick, smelly sweat in the armpits
options.C: Helping cool down the body through sweat evaporation
options.D: Releasing watery fluid onto the skin

explanation: Spot on! Armpit and groin sweat comes from apocrine glands, while your ordinary (eccrine) glands make watery sweat all over to keep you cool. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why do many Nigerian families prefer home health care for their sick relatives?

options.A: To completely avoid paying any hospital bills
options.B: To comply with mandatory national health insurance rules
options.C: To access advanced surgical theaters at home
options.D: To bypass long hospital queues and get personal attention

explanation: Spot on! Families love home care because it helps them dodge long hospital waits and gives their loved one undivided attention.

question: What is the correct action a nurse should take before applying a new dose of a topical skin cream?

options.A: Shave all body hair from the area regardless of the medication type
options.B: Scrub the skin hard with alcohol wipes to remove the stratum corneum
options.C: Gently clean the skin to remove old medication residue and dirt
options.D: Apply a thick layer of plastic wrap over the old cream without cleaning

explanation: Cleaning away old residue and debris ensures proper contact and prevents chemical buildup or irritation on the skin surface. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h6)

question: What is a direct result of poor nutrition in an older adult going through rehabilitation?

options.A: Delayed wound healing and increased muscle weakness
options.B: Enhanced immune system function
options.C: Instant recovery from chronic stroke symptoms
options.D: Rapid muscle growth and increased strength

explanation: Brilliant! Without good food and protein, the body simply doesn't have the fuel to repair tissues or build strength.

question: Which type of precaution requires the use of a negative-pressure room?

options.A: Droplet precautions
options.B: Airborne precautions
options.C: Standard precautions
options.D: Contact precautions

explanation: Airborne precautions require special negative-pressure ventilation to keep infectious particles from escaping into the hallway. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why does semen briefly thicken right after ejaculation before turning watery again?

options.A: To prevent the sperm from leaking out immediately
options.B: To block the urinary bladder completely
options.C: To make the sperm travel much faster through the testes
options.D: To kill off any weak sperm cells present in the fluid

explanation: The initial clotting keeps everything securely in place, and then it liquefies so the sperm can start their journey upward. Clever design!

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in clinical practice?

options.A: To speed up the administration of intravenous medications
options.B: To prevent harm to patients, health workers, and the community
options.C: To eliminate the need for wearing gloves during procedures
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing medical syringes

explanation: Injection safety encompasses measures that protect the patient receiving the injection, the nurse administering it, and the surrounding community from hazardous waste. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is a major economic reason why impoverished households practice child marriage?

options.A: Complying with mandatory government taxation policies for unmarried girls
options.B: Securing high-paying white-collar employment for the young bride
options.C: Funding the higher education of male siblings in the family
options.D: Reducing household financial burdens through bride price or fewer dependents

explanation: Extreme poverty pushes some families to marry off young daughters to ease household expenses and sometimes gain financial help through bride wealth.

question: What is the best way to interpret a child's weight measurement in a clinic?

options.A: Averaging the weight reading with the mother's weight
options.B: Plotting the measurement on a growth chart to observe the growth trend over time
options.C: Checking if the weight matches the child's shoe size and hair color
options.D: Comparing the child's weight directly to the average weight of an adult

explanation: A single number doesn't tell the whole story. Seeing how the weight tracks on a growth curve over months shows the true picture of health!

question: What is the correct step to take the moment a sharps container hits its fill line?

options.A: Leave the lid open for the next shift to use
options.B: Press the contents down firmly with your hand
options.C: Lock the lid securely and prepare for disposal
options.D: Empty the contents into a regular black bin

explanation: Locking the lid right away stops accidental spills and keeps protruding needles from injuring anyone.

question: What is the main purpose of assessment tools like the Minimum Data Set (MDS) in long-term care?

options.A: To systematically evaluate resident health status and functional capacity
options.B: To replace the need for daily nursing vital sign documentation
options.C: To bill insurance companies for emergency room visits
options.D: To determine the discharge date for acute hospital recovery

explanation: Well done! Tools like the MDS give us a clear, organized way to track how a resident's physical and mental abilities change over time.

question: A woman who took oral medications for Type 2 diabetes for five years becomes pregnant. How is her condition classified?

options.A: Transient pregnancy hyperglycemia
options.B: Pregestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Secondary placental diabetes

explanation: Because she had diagnosed diabetes and took medications before getting pregnant, her condition is classified as pregestational diabetes. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h2)

question: You hear a call bell ring, but right at that moment, another patient starts struggling to breathe. What should you do first?

options.A: Finish charting at the desk before responding to either
options.B: Assess the patient who is struggling to breathe
options.C: Answer the call bell immediately to find out what is needed
options.D: Ask a visitor to check on the patient in the room

explanation: Brilliant! ABC comes first. A breathing difficulty is a life-threatening emergency that always beats a general call bell.

question: A hospitalized patient with chronic bronchitis is struggling to breathe and their oxygen is dropping. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.A: Elevate the head of the bed and assess breathing status
options.B: Wait for the environmental agency to clear the outdoor air
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately so they can get fresh air
options.D: Encourage the patient to perform heavy physical exercise

explanation: Spot on! Always start by positioning the patient to help them breathe better and checking their status before jumping to other steps.

question: What is the main difference between a pathogen's 'reservoir' and its 'source'?

options.A: A reservoir is found inside the human body, while a source is always environmental
options.B: There is no difference between the two terms in clinical epidemiology
options.C: A reservoir only contains viruses, while a source only transmits bacterial infections
options.D: A reservoir is the natural habitat of a pathogen, while a source is the immediate point of transmission

explanation: A reservoir is where the germ lives comfortably and multiplies (like its home), whereas the source is the exact thing that hands it over to you.

question: What does true professional accountability mean for a nurse leader?

options.A: Take personal ownership of actions, decisions, and outcomes
options.B: Blame junior staff whenever a clinical mistake happens
options.C: Keep all patient safety data hidden from the public
options.D: Delegate all disciplinary actions to hospital administrators

explanation: Accountability means standing tall and owning your choices—taking credit when things go well, and accepting responsibility when things go wrong.

question: What is the main goal of medication reconciliation during a patient's hospital stay?

options.A: To reduce the number of nurses required on duty
options.B: To return unused drugs back to the pharmaceutical company
options.C: To calculate the total cost of drugs used in the ward
options.D: To compare past and current medications to prevent errors

explanation: Medication reconciliation ensures that home medications and new hospital orders match properly without dangerous gaps or overlaps. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h4)

question: A country is suffering from massive crop failures due to drought and conflict. What is the best way to handle this?

options.A: Waiting until the crisis resolves itself without altering agricultural policies
options.B: Multi-sector collaboration combining government reserves, NGO outreach, and international aid
options.C: Leaving food distribution entirely to local retail supermarkets without outside help
options.D: Banning all international humanitarian organizations from entering the country

explanation: Big crises need teamwork! When governments, local NGOs, and international agencies join forces, they can save lives much faster.

question: Which serious side effect should nurses watch out for in patients taking fertility drugs for IVF ovarian stimulation?

options.A: Sudden permanent hair loss
options.B: Chronic iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
options.D: Complete cessation of urine output from kidney failure

explanation: Brilliant! OHSS happens when ovaries swell up and leak fluid, and a sharp nurse spots this early. You're thinking like a pro!

question: A family caring for a young adult with a spinal cord injury insists on doing everything for them, refusing to let them try dressing themselves. What is this family showing?

options.A: Harmful overprotection
options.B: Caregiver neglect
options.C: Sibling rivalry
options.D: Professional detachment

explanation: You nailed it! While out of love, doing everything for a patient stops them from building confidence and independence.

question: What is the golden rule when a nurse has to break tragic news of a death to family members?

options.A: Use clear, direct, and compassionate language
options.B: Ask another family member to break the news
options.C: Use complex medical terms to soften the blow
options.D: Delay the information until they stop crying

explanation: That's right! Being clear and direct avoids any confusion, ensuring the family understands the reality while feeling your compassion.

question: What actually drives water to move passively across the wall of the intestine?

options.A: Active water pumps on the enterocyte membrane
options.B: Changes in core body temperature
options.C: Direct muscle contractions of the villi
options.D: Osmotic gradients created by solute absorption

explanation: Water loves to follow the crowd! As the gut pumps in salts and sugars, water naturally flows right along with them through osmosis.

question: What does antimicrobial resistance mean?

options.A: The human immune system destroys all beneficial bacteria
options.B: Microbes change and survive treatment with standard medications
options.C: Antibiotics lose their expiration date while on the shelf
options.D: Patients develop an allergic reaction to powerful drugs

explanation: Resistance happens when germs mutate or adapt so that drugs that used to kill them no longer work. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h4)

question: What event signals the secondary oocyte to finish its final cell division (meiosis II)?

options.A: A sharp rise in vaginal pH
options.B: The shedding of the uterine lining
options.C: The process of implantation
options.D: The entry of a sperm cell

explanation: Correct! The egg stays paused until a sperm touches down, providing the exact wakeup call it needs to complete its division.

question: What is the main job of myosin light chain kinase (MLCK)?

options.A: To pump calcium back into storage sites
options.B: To break down ATP for cellular energy
options.C: To connect adjacent muscle fibers together
options.D: To phosphorylate myosin heads so they can bind to actin

explanation: Think of MLCK as the activator: it adds a chemical tag (phosphate) to the myosin head so it knows it's go-time and can grab onto actin!

question: What are the common signs of a Chlamydia infection in a young female?

options.A: Painless hard sores on the palms
options.B: High fever and generalized skin rash
options.C: Severe joint swelling and stiffness
options.D: Mucopurulent discharge and dysuria

explanation: Spot on! Chlamydia often causes irritation in the cervix and urethra, leading to unusual discharge and painful urination (dysuria).

question: A patient stays home from work, complains of body aches to their partner, and rests in bed. Which stage of illness behavior is this?

options.A: Dependent client role
options.B: Assuming the sick role
options.C: Recovery stage
options.D: Medical care contact stage

explanation: Spot on! At this stage, the person accepts that they are sick, gets support from loved ones, and takes a break from their normal daily duties.

question: What happens when an anticholinergic drug successfully binds to a receptor on the bladder?

options.A: The muscle contracts harder to empty the bladder completely
options.B: Normal muscle contractions are blocked, preventing spasms
options.C: Urine production in the kidneys stops temporarily
options.D: Blood flow to the urinary tract increases significantly

explanation: By occupying the spot, the drug blocks acetylcholine from turning on the squeeze switch, giving the bladder a chance to rest.

question: How do nurses directly help keep drugs safe after they are already released to the public?

options.A: By manufacturing safer alternative medications in hospital pharmacies
options.B: By setting the official market price for all new pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: By reporting unexpected and unusual drug reactions to authorities
options.D: By conducting clinical trials on animals in hospital laboratories

explanation: Nurses are at the bedside every day, making you the crucial eyes and ears for reporting strange side effects and protecting the public!

question: Which of these is a key nursing duty to help prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia?

options.A: Giving strong antibiotics to every intubated patient
options.B: Keeping the head of the bed completely flat
options.C: Changing the ventilator machine every hour
options.D: Performing regular oral care with antiseptic solutions

explanation: Mouth hygiene is huge! Keeping the mouth clean stops nasty bacteria from multiplying and sliding down into the lungs.

question: Which of the following symptoms should a nurse instruct a client to report immediately as a red-flag warning?

options.A: Sudden severe pelvic pain or excessive bleeding
options.B: Mild fatigue after completing a normal workday
options.C: Minor bloating before the onset of menses
options.D: Slight breast tenderness during the menstrual cycle

explanation: Sudden severe pain or hemorrhage can indicate acute surgical emergencies like a ruptured cyst, ectopic pregnancy, or severe post-op bleeding. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h8)

question: Which blood vessel brings blood directly into the glomerulus for filtering?

options.A: Peritubular capillary
options.B: Efferent arteriole
options.C: Renal vein
options.D: Afferent arteriole

explanation: Spot on! Think of the 'A' in Afferent as 'Arriving'—it brings blood into the glomerulus, while the efferent arteriole carries it away.

question: Why is it important to warn older adult patients about dizziness while on these drugs?

options.A: To explain why their blood pressure will drop to zero
options.B: To ensure they avoid all forms of physical exercise
options.C: To prepare them for permanent balance loss
options.D: To help prevent accidental falls and injuries at home

explanation: Dizziness and blurry vision make falls a real danger for elderly patients, making safety warnings a key part of your nursing care.

question: What does the acronym NEAT stand for in energy expenditure?

options.A: Non-exercise activity thermogenesis
options.B: Nutritional energy and tissue
options.C: Net enteral absorption time
options.D: Normal electrolyte and acid test

explanation: NEAT stands for non-exercise activity thermogenesis, covering all daily movements outside of formal workouts. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h4)

question: How should a home care patient safely throw away used insulin needles and lancets?

options.A: Directly into the household kitchen garbage bin
options.B: In a rigid, puncture-resistant sharps container
options.C: In an open plastic grocery bag tied at the top
options.D: Flushed immediately down the indoor toilet

explanation: Sharps containers prevent accidental needle pricks for family members, pets, and waste collectors handling the trash.

question: Why does missing ovulation while having ongoing oestrogen exposure put the uterine lining at risk?

options.A: Without progesterone to balance it, oestrogen causes the uterine lining to overgrow
options.B: The ovaries stop producing all hormones, causing the uterus to shrink rapidly
options.C: Lack of ovulation permanently closes the cervical opening against fluids
options.D: Anovulatory cycles force toxic blood to back up into the abdominal cavity

explanation: Think of progesterone as the brake pedal for oestrogen. Without it, the uterine lining keeps building up without shedding properly.

question: What color and look does a normal, healthy eardrum (tympanic membrane) usually have?

options.A: Pearly gray and see-through (translucent)
options.B: Bright red and solid
options.C: Dark blue with fluid inside
options.D: Yellow, thick, and full of pus

explanation: A healthy eardrum is shiny, pearly gray, and translucent, letting you peek at the middle ear structures underneath.

question: What is the primary function of cerebrospinal fluid?

options.A: To transmit electrical signals across synapses
options.B: To cushion the brain and provide nutritional support
options.C: To produce red blood cells for nervous tissue
options.D: To cool down the body during a high fever

explanation: CSF acts as a shock-absorbing liquid cushion while also nourishing the central nervous system tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h7)

question: A nurse manager holds a staff meeting to ask everyone for ideas on how to fix the weekend scheduling roster. What leadership style is being used?

options.A: Coercive
options.B: Democratic
options.C: Laissez-faire
options.D: Autocratic

explanation: Asking the team for input and involving them in decisions is the hallmark of democratic leadership. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h5)

question: What do we call any environmental factor or substance that causes birth defects in an unborn baby?

options.A: Pathogen
options.B: Carcinogen
options.C: Teratogen
options.D: Allergen

explanation: Spot on! Teratogens are agents like certain drugs, radiation, or infections that can interfere with normal prenatal development. You're making great progress!

question: What is a common effect on an infant if a breastfeeding mother consumes excessive amounts of caffeine?

options.A: Severe weight gain and fluid retention
options.B: Jitteriness and sleep disturbances
options.C: Uncontrolled drowsiness and deep coma
options.D: Immediate development of infant jaundice

explanation: Babies process caffeine very slowly, so too much of it from breast milk can make them restless and unable to sleep. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h7)

question: A researcher checks past patient charts from five years ago to find links between smoking and lung disease. What study type is this?

options.A: Retrospective study
options.B: Qualitative interview study
options.C: Prospective study
options.D: Cross-sectional study

explanation: You got it! Retrospective studies look backward ('retro') at records of past events to find the background or causes of current health conditions. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is home health care such an exciting shift in modern nursing?

options.A: It moves professional care from large hospitals back into the community
options.B: It focuses only on domestic chores rather than medical tasks
options.C: It completely replaces the need for doctors and clinics
options.D: It removes all responsibilities from family caregivers

explanation: Spot on! Instead of keeping everyone stuck in hospital wards, home care brings the healing right into the patient's familiar home environment.

question: Why is it important for the body to release hormones in pulses?

options.A: It ensures constant, unvarying blood pressure all day
options.B: It prevents receptor down-regulation and desensitization
options.C: It stops the nervous system from sending electrical signals
options.D: It triggers immediate humoral stimulation in the pancreas

explanation: If cells are flooded with hormones non-stop, they get 'numb' to them. Pulsing keeps the cell receptors fresh and listening!

question: Why is simply giving people health information (one-way sharing) often not enough on its own?

options.A: It automatically causes confusion among patients
options.B: It requires too many expensive laboratory tests
options.C: It fails to address deep-seated social norms and personal habits
options.D: It can only be delivered by senior medical doctors

explanation: You got it! Just telling people what to do isn't enough; changing human habits and cultural routines takes real engagement and ongoing support.

question: What crucial safety rule must be kept in mind when treating a patient infected with Taenia solium?

options.A: Giving the medication exclusively through an intravenous infusion
options.B: Ensuring the patient fasts completely for one week prior to dosing
options.C: Preventing the patient from swallowing shed eggs to avoid cysticercosis
options.D: Keeping the patient isolated in a negative pressure room

explanation: Brilliant! If the patient vomits or has poor hygiene during treatment, they might accidentally swallow T. solium eggs and develop dangerous tissue cysts.

question: Why must pregnant women attend antenatal clinics even when they feel completely fine?

options.A: Pregnant women are legally required to visit the clinic every single week
options.B: It is impossible to eat a balanced diet without clinic supervision
options.C: Clinics require attendance records to secure international funding
options.D: Dangerous conditions like high blood pressure can develop without early warning signs

explanation: Exactly! Silent issues like pre-eclampsia or anemia can build up inside without any obvious signs at first. Routine checks keep both mum and baby safe.

question: The doctor orders Paracetamol 500 mg. Pharmacy sends Paracetamol scored tablets of 250 mg each. How many tablets will you give?

options.A: 1 tablet
options.B: 0.5 tablets
options.C: 4 tablets
options.D: 2 tablets

explanation: Using Desired over Have: (500 mg / 250 mg) × 1 tablet = 2 tablets. Perfect!

question: Why must a good management plan have a broad scope?

options.A: To eliminate the need for inter-departmental communication
options.B: To anticipate how changes in one department affect other units
options.C: To make the planning document look impressive to inspectors
options.D: To ensure every single employee works overtime every week

explanation: Hospital units are closely connected. A comprehensive plan looks at the entire system rather than isolating just one ward.

question: How do barrier methods of contraception primarily prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By stopping the ovaries from releasing eggs
options.B: By altering the lining of the uterus
options.C: By thickening the natural cervical mucus
options.D: By physically blocking sperm from meeting the egg

explanation: Spot on! Barrier methods act like a physical shield that keeps sperm from traveling up to meet the egg. You've got this!

question: In community health nursing, who is considered your primary client?

options.A: The individual patient in a hospital bed
options.B: The entire community or population
options.C: The medical doctor in charge of the ward
options.D: The administrative management of the hospital

explanation: You've got this! While hospital nursing focuses on one patient at a time, community health nursing looks at the big picture and cares for the whole population.

question: Why do we position the patient in the left lateral Sims' position for a rectal washout?

options.A: It follows the natural anatomical curve of the lower colon
options.B: It prevents the patient from falling asleep during the task
options.C: It completely stops normal peristaltic movement in the gut
options.D: It keeps the patient's head elevated above the heart level

explanation: The lower part of the colon curves down toward the left side, making the left lateral position the smoothest and easiest way to insert the tube.

question: Why is a structured handover important when transferring a patient to the postnatal ward?

options.A: It allows the delivery room staff to take a longer break
options.B: It replaces the need for keeping a written clinical chart
options.C: It forces the patient to retell her entire medical history
options.D: It ensures vital information and ongoing risks are clearly communicated

explanation: A structured handover prevents important clinical details from being missed, ensuring safe continuity of care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h9)

question: Why is a good referral system so important for a client's reproductive rights?

options.A: It gives nurses full authority to choose which contraceptive a client must use
options.B: It forces clients to accept permanent contraceptive methods
options.C: It prevents clients from visiting traditional birth attendants
options.D: It ensures clients can access their preferred method even if local stock runs out

explanation: Clients have the right to choose what works for their bodies. If your clinic runs out of a specific supply, referring them elsewhere protects that choice!

question: What is another name for a hospital-acquired infection?

options.A: Congenital disease
options.B: Chronic ailment
options.C: Idiopathic condition
options.D: Nosocomial infection

explanation: Infections caught while receiving medical care in a hospital or clinic are formally called nosocomial infections. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the main difference between a study conclusion and a recommendation?

options.A: Conclusions are optional, while recommendations are mandatory for all papers
options.B: Conclusions use statistics, while recommendations use personal opinions
options.C: Conclusions summarize main findings, while recommendations suggest future actions
options.D: Conclusions appear in the introduction, while recommendations are in the abstract

explanation: A conclusion wraps up what you found out, while a recommendation suggests what should be done next in practice.

question: Which of these is NOT a normal challenge faced by public health institutions?

options.A: Excessive financial profits and private wealth accumulation
options.B: Bureaucratic delays in procuring medical supplies
options.C: Brain drain of experienced healthcare workers
options.D: Infrastructure decay and power supply failures

explanation: You nailed it! Public hospitals rarely swim in extra cash or private wealth; rather, they usually struggle with underfunding and resource shortages.

question: What is a major warning sign that a young adolescent girl is at risk of early marriage?

options.A: Sudden dropout from school and withdrawal from youth activities
options.B: Employment as a registered healthcare worker
options.C: Frequent participation in community health advocacy
options.D: Enrolment in advanced vocational training programs

explanation: Leaving school early and disappearing from youth groups are classic red flags that a young girl is about to be married off.

question: Why is charting the details of an eye irrigation so important in the patient's record?

options.A: It proves to the pharmacy department that sterile supplies were wasted
options.B: It provides a clear legal record of solution amount, duration, and patient response
options.C: It prevents the patient from receiving any further medical bills
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will regain full vision by tomorrow

explanation: Good documentation protects both you and the patient by proving exactly what care was given and how the patient responded.

question: An administrator says 'no' to your staffing proposal because it costs too much. What is your best next move?

options.A: Organize a violent protest outside the administrative office
options.B: Prepare constructive evidence showing long-term cost savings and safety
options.C: Threaten the administrator with a media boycott
options.D: Abandon the advocacy campaign immediately and give up

explanation: Smart thinking! Coming back with solid proof that your idea improves safety and saves money in the long run is way more effective than getting upset.

question: What is a major challenge that family caregivers often face when looking after a sick relative at home?

options.A: Burnout and physical exhaustion
options.B: Over-staffing by professional nurses
options.C: Excessive financial compensation
options.D: Too much free time and boredom

explanation: Exactly right. Caregiver fatigue is real! Looking after a loved one without a break can easily lead to physical and emotional burnout.

question: Why do nurses recommend using an ordinary cup instead of a feeding bottle for giving liquids to older infants?

options.A: Cups are much easier to clean and lower the risk of bacterial infections
options.B: Using bottles interferes with the natural development of the jawbone
options.C: Cups encourage the infant to drink larger volumes of liquid at one time
options.D: Infants cannot swallow liquids properly from a bottle after six months

explanation: Feeding bottles have tricky nooks and crannies that trap germs and are tough to sterilize. Cups are simple to wash and keep babies much safer from tummy bugs!

question: A patient tells you they are terrified they might die. Which response shows therapeutic communication?

options.A: Leaving the room immediately to let them calm down on their own
options.B: Changing the subject quickly so the patient doesn't start crying
options.C: Validating their feelings and offering a supportive, listening presence
options.D: Telling them not to worry because modern medicine can cure anything

explanation: Just sitting with a frightened patient and saying 'I am here for you' is sometimes the most powerful medicine you can offer.

question: In Herzberg's theory, what happens when a workplace 'hygiene factor' is missing?

options.A: It causes job dissatisfaction
options.B: It encourages nurses to work longer hours
options.C: It has absolutely no effect on staff
options.D: It instantly boosts employee creativity

explanation: Correct! Hygiene factors (like basic pay or a decent work environment) won't necessarily make you jump for joy, but if they are missing, you will definitely be unhappy.

question: Which of these details is NOT necessary to chart after giving a rectal medication?

options.A: Any local discomfort or side effects noted
options.B: The patient's favorite hobby or pastime
options.C: The exact time and date of administration
options.D: The specific name and dose of the drug

explanation: Personal hobbies have nothing to do with clinical charting. Always focus on the drug name, dose, time, and patient response!

question: Why is it smart for a nurse to involve religious leaders and local heads in a community health plan?

options.A: To dispense prescription antibiotics to villagers
options.B: To gain community buy-in and policy support
options.C: To diagnose complex medical surgical conditions
options.D: To audit hospital financial expenditure records

explanation: Spot on! Local leaders have great influence over the people, so having their backing helps the community welcome new health programs.
